title: Bishop colours and blocked paths
objectives: Recognize that each bishop stays on one square colour for the whole game

steps.text: A bishop that starts on a light square stays on light squares forever — it can never reach a dark square. The same is true for a dark-squared bishop.

steps.prompt: A bishop that starts on a dark square can eventually reach a light square.

feedback.default: Diagonal moves always keep a bishop on the same colour square for the entire game.

steps.successExplanation: Right — a bishop's whole diagonal world is fixed by which colour square it started on.

steps.prompt: Find the bishop's legal move that captures the black pawn.

feedback.default: The bishop can slide diagonally right up to and capture the pawn on c6 — but it can't go past it.

steps.successExplanation: Bxc6 captures the pawn. The bishop stops exactly where the first piece in its path sits.

steps.prompt: Capture the knight with your bishop.

feedback.default: Look along the bishop's open diagonal — it can't cross its own pawn on f5, but the other diagonal is completely clear.

steps.successExplanation: Bxb1 captures the knight. The e4-b1 diagonal was completely clear, even though the bishop's own pawn blocks the diagonal toward f5.

steps.summary: Bishops move and capture diagonally, any distance, but always stay on one square colour for the whole game and stop dead at the first piece — friend or foe — in their path.
